cases.ac: AC-1: Stone block: clicks 1-2 show crack stages, click 3 removes it and +1 stone inventory; HUD updates.
cases.oracle: In the node:vm sandbox seed a stone (hardness 3) cell at (x,y). hitCell(x,y) hits 1 and 2 each leave the cell present with __test.damage.get(cellKey) === hits (1, then 2) and a crack overlay at stage hits-1 drawn as a pure function of (x, y, stage); the 3rd hitCell removes the cell, deletes its damage entry, and __test.inventory.stone === 1; the HUD count rendered via __test.setState reflects stone count 1. Asserted through the real hitCell/pointer path via the injected __test hook, not by re-implementing game rules.

cases.ac: AC-2: Grass block: single click removes, +1 grass inventory.
cases.oracle: A single hitCell(x,y) on a grass (hardness 1) cell removes the cell in that one hit, increments __test.inventory.grass to 1, and leaves no damage-map entry for the cell.

cases.ac: AC-3: Placing from palette decrements that type's inventory and refuses at 0.
cases.oracle: With __test.inventory[type] === n > 0, selecting that palette type and placing decrements the counter to n-1 and writes the cell. Then with the counter at 0, a place attempt is refused before any mutation: the grid cell is unchanged and the counter stays 0.

cases.ac: AC-4: Reload persists both the world and the inventory (localStorage).
cases.oracle: After digging and placing, localStorage[STORAGE_KEY] holds a v2 blob {version: 2, cells, inventory} with non-negative integer counts for block keys 1..4; loading that same blob into a fresh sandbox restores identical cells and inventory, and the transient damage map is empty after reload (resets, not persisted).

cleanup.environment: Stateless `node --test` run: the game script is loaded into a node:vm sandbox with stubbed DOM/canvas/localStorage per subtest; no server, browser or resident process is started, so there is nothing to tear down.
cleanup.data: localStorage is an in-memory sandbox stub under key minicraft-grid-v1; no fixture is written to disk, no live configuration (including .claude/settings.json) is touched — no data cleanup required.
